facing the same direction\n485:     if (triI.normal().dot(triJ.normal()) > 0.99f) return ZERO;\n486: \n487:     val_t kij = ZERO;\n488: \n489:     for (int r = 0; r < NUM_RAYS; ++r) {\n490: cosPhiJ = cosPhi(-v, triJ.normal());\n501: \n502:         if (cosPhiI <= ZERO || cosPhiJ <= ZERO) continue;\n503: \n504:         kij += (cosPhiI * cosPhiJ) / (PI * distSqr);\n505:     }\n506: \n507: {}\n\n    Vec3 operator+(const Vec3& o) const { return {x + o.x, y + o.y, z + o.z}; }\n    Vec3 operator-(const Vec3& o) const { return {x - o.x, y - o.y, z - o.z}; }\n    Vec3 operator*(val_t s) const { return {x * s, y * s, z * s}; }\n    Vec3 operator/(val_t s) const { return {x / s, y / s, z / s}; }\n    Vec3 operator-() const { return {-x, -y, -z}; }\n\n    val_t dot(const Vec3& o) const { return x * o.x + y * o.y + z * o.z; }\n    Vec3 cross(const Vec3& o) const {\n        return {y * o.z - z * o.y, z * o.x - x * o.z, x * o.y - y * o.x};\n    }\n\n    val_t squaredNorm() const { return x * x + y * y + z * z; }\n    val_t norm() const { return std::sqrt(squaredNorm()); }\n    Vec3 normalized() const {\n        val_t n = norm();\n        return n > EPSILON ? *this / n : Vec3();\n    }\n\n    bool operator==(const Vec3& o) const {\n        return std::abs(x - o.x) < EPSILON && std::abs(y - o.y) < EPSILON && std::abs(z - o.z) < EPSILON;\n    }\n};\n\nstruct Triangle {\n    Vec3 a, b, c;\n    Vec3 _normal;\n\n    Triangle() = default;\n    Triangle(const Vec3& a, const Vec3& b, const Vec3& c)\n        : a(a), b(b), c(c), _normal((b - a).cross(c - a).normalized()) {}\n\n    Vec3 center() const { return (a + b + c) / 3.0f; }\n    Vec3 normal() const { return _normal; }\n\n    val_t area() const {\n        Vec3 ab = b - a;\n        Vec3 ac = c - a;\n        return 0.5f * ab.cross(ac).norm();\n    }\n\n    bool operator==(const Triangle& o) const { return a == o.a && b == o.b && c == o.c; }\n};\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Triangle-Box Overlap Test (for octree construction)\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Separating axis test for triangle-box overlap\nbool triangleBoxOverlap(const Vec3& boxCenter, const Vec3& boxHalfSize, const Triangle& tri) {\n    // Translate triangle to box center\n    Vec3 v0 = tri.a - boxCenter;\n    Vec3 v1 = tri.b - boxCenter;\n    Vec3 v2 = tri.c - boxCenter;\n\n    // Triangle edges\n    Vec3 e0 = v1 - v0;\n    Vec3 e1 = v2 - v1;\n    Vec3 e2 = v0 - v2;\n\n    // Test box normals (AABB axes)\n    auto minMax3 = [](val_t a, val_t b, val_t c) {\n        return std::make_pair(std::min({a, b, c}), std::max({a, b, c}));\n    };\n\n    auto [minX, maxX] = minMax3(v0.x, v1.x, v2.x);\n    if (minX > boxHalfSize.x || maxX < -boxHalfSize.x) return false;\n\n    auto [minY, maxY] = minMax3(v0.y, v1.y, v2.y);\n    if (minY > boxHalfSize.y || maxY < -boxHalfSize.y) return false;\n\n    auto [minZ, maxZ] = minMax3(v0.z, v1.z, v2.z);\n    if (minZ > boxHalfSize.z || maxZ < -boxHalfSize.z) return false;\n\n    // Test triangle normal\n    Vec3 triNormal = e0.cross(e1);\n    val_t d = triNormal.dot(v0);\n    val_t r = boxHalfSize.x * std::abs(triNormal.x) +\n              boxHalfSize.y * std::abs(triNormal.y) +\n              boxHalfSize.z * std::abs(triNormal.z);\n    if (std::abs(d) > r) return false;\n\n    // Test 9 edge cross products\n    auto testAxis = [&](const Vec3& axis) {\n        val_t p0 = axis.dot(v0);\n        val_t p1 = axis.dot(v1);\n        val_t p2 = axis.dot(v2);\n        val_t r = boxHalfSize.x * std::abs(axis.x) +\n                  boxHalfSize.y * std::abs(axis.y) +\n                  boxHalfSize.z * std::abs(axis.z);\n        auto [minP, maxP] = minMax3(p0, p1, p2);\n        return !(minP > r || maxP < -r);\n    };\n\n    Vec3 axes[3] = {{1,0,0}, {0,1,0}, {0,0,1}};\n    Vec3 edges[3] = {e0, e1, e2};\n    for (const auto& axis : axes) {\n        for (const auto& edge : edges) {\n            Vec3 crossAxis = axis.cross(edge);\n            if (crossAxis.squaredNorm() > EPSILON) {\n                if (!testAxis(crossAxis)) return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Octree for Spatial Acceleration\n// ============================================================================\n\nconstexpr size_t MAX_OCTREE_TRIS = 8;\nconstexpr val_t MAX_OCTREE_LEAF_SIZE = 0.5f;\n\nclass Octree {\npublic:\n    Vec3 minBound, maxBound;\n    Vec3 halfExtent, center;\n    std::unique_ptr<Octree> children[8];\n    std::vector<size_t> triangleIndices;  // Indices into the global triangle list\n    const std::vector<Triangle>* allTriangles;  // Pointer to all triangles\n\n    Octree() : allTriangles(nullptr) {}\n\n    void build(const std::vector<Triangle>& triangles) {\n        allTriangles = &triangles;\n        if (triangles.empty()) return;\n\n        // Compute bounding box\n        minBound = triangles[0].a;\n        maxBound = triangles[0].a;\n        for (const auto& tri : triangles) {\n            for (const auto* v : {&tri.a, &tri.b, &tri.c}) {\n                minBound.x = std::min(minBound.x, v->x);\n                minBound.y = std::min(minBound.y, v->y);\n                minBound.z = std::min(minBound.z, v->z);\n                maxBound.x = std::max(maxBound.x, v->x);\n                maxBound.y = std::max(maxBound.y, v->y);\n                maxBound.z = std::max(maxBound.z, v->z);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Collect all indices\n        std::vector<size_t> allIndices(triangles.size());\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < triangles.size(); ++i) allIndices[i] = i;\n\n        buildNode(allIndices, minBound, maxBound);\n    }\n\nprivate:\n    void buildNode(const std::vector<size_t>& indices, const Vec3& nodeMin, const Vec3& nodeMax) {\n        minBound = nodeMin;\n        maxBound = nodeMax;\n        halfExtent = (maxBound - minBound) * 0.5f;\n        center = (minBound + maxBound) * 0.5f;\n\n        // If few enough triangles or too small, make this a leaf\n        if (indices.size() <= MAX_OCTREE_TRIS ||\n            (maxBound - minBound).norm() < MAX_OCTREE_LEAF_SIZE) {\n            triangleIndices = indices;\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Subdivide into 8 children\n        Vec3 childHalfSize = halfExtent * 0.5f;\n        std::vector<size_t> childIndices[8];\n\n        for (size_t idx : indices) {\n            const Triangle& tri = (*allTriangles)[idx];\n\n            // Check which children this triangle overlaps\n            for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n                Vec3 childCenter = center;\n                childCenter.x += (i & 1) ? childHalfSize.x : -childHalfSize.x;\n                childCenter.y += (i & 2) ? childHalfSize.y : -childHalfSize.y;\n                childCenter.z += (i & 4) ? childHalfSize.z : -childHalfSize.z;\n\n                if (triangleBoxOverlap(childCenter, childHalfSize, tri)) {\n                    childIndices[i].push_back(idx);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Check if we can't split further (all triangles in one child)\n        bool canSplit = false;\n        for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n            if (!childIndices[i].empty() && childIndices[i].size() < indices.size()) {\n                canSplit = true;\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if (!canSplit) {\n            triangleIndices = indices;\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Build children\n        for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n            if (!childIndices[i].empty()) {\n                Vec3 childMin = center;\n                Vec3 childMax = center;\n                childMin.x = (i & 1) ? center.x : minBound.x;\n                childMax.x = (i & 1) ? maxBound.x : center.x;\n                childMin.y = (i & 2) ? center.y : minBound.y;\n                childMax.y = (i & 2) ? maxBound.y : center.y;\n                childMin.z = (i & 4) ? center.z : minBound.z;\n                childMax.z = (i & 4) ? maxBound.z : center.z;\n\n                children[i] = std::make_unique<Octree>();\n                children[i]->allTriangles = allTriangles;\n                children[i]->buildNode(childIndices[i], childMin, childMax);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\npublic:\n    // Check if a ray intersects this node's bounding box\n    bool rayIntersectsBox(const Vec3& p1, const Vec3& p2) const {\n        Vec3 d = (p2 - p1) * 0.5f;\n        Vec3 c = p1 + d - center;\n        Vec3 ad = {std::abs(d.x), std::abs(d.y), std::abs(d.z)};\n\n        if (std::abs(c.x) > halfExtent.x + ad.x) return false;\n        if (std::abs(c.y) > halfExtent.y + ad.y) return false;\n        if (std::abs(c.z) > halfExtent.z + ad.z) return false;\n\n        if (std::abs(d.y * c.z - d.z * c.y) > halfExtent.y * ad.z + halfExtent.z * ad.y + EPSILON) return false;\n        if (std::abs(d.z * c.x - d.x * c.z) > halfExtent.z * ad.x + halfExtent.x * ad.z + EPSILON) return false;\n        if (std::abs(d.x * c.y - d.y * c.x) > halfExtent.x * ad.y + halfExtent.y * ad.x + EPSILON) return false;\n\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    // Apply a function to all triangles potentially intersecting the ray\n    // Returns true if the function returns true for any triangle\n    template<typename Func>\n    bool applyToTris(const Vec3& p1, const Vec3& p2, Func&& func) const {\n        // If leaf node, check triangles directly\n        if (!triangleIndices.empty()) {\n            for (size_t idx : triangleIndices) {\n                if (func(idx, (*allTriangles)[idx])) return true;\n            }\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Otherwise, descend to children\n        for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n            if (children[i] && children[i]->rayIntersectsBox(p1, p2)) {\n                if (children[i]->applyToTris(p1, p2, func)) return true;\n            }\n        }\n        return false;\n    }\n};\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Mesh Generation: Icosphere\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Generate an icosphere by subdividing an icosahedron\nclass IcosphereMesh {\npublic:\n    std::vector<Triangle> triangles;\n\n    IcosphereMesh(int subdivisions, val_t radius) {\n        // Initial icosahedron vertices\n        const val_t t = (1.0f + std::sqrt(5.0f)) / 2.0f;\n\n        std::vector<Vec3> vertices = {\n            Vec3(-1,  t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 1,  t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3(-1, -t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 1, -t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0, -1,  t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0,  1,  t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0, -1, -t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0,  1, -t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( t,  0, -1).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( t,  0,  1).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3(-t,  0, -1).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3(-t,  0,  1).normalized() * radius\n        };\n\n        // Initial icosahedron faces (20 triangles)\n        std::vector<std::array<idx_t, 3>> faces = {\n            {0, 11, 5}, {0, 5, 1}, {0, 1, 7}, {0, 7, 10}, {0, 10, 11},\n            {1, 5, 9}, {5, 11, 4}, {11, 10, 2}, {10, 7, 6}, {7, 1, 8},\n            {3, 9, 4}, {3, 4, 2}, {3, 2, 6}, {3, 6, 8}, {3, 8, 9},\n            {4, 9, 5}, {2, 4, 11}, {6, 2, 10}, {8, 6, 7}, {9, 8, 1}\n        };\n\n        // Subdivide\n        for (int i = 0; i < subdivisions; ++i) {\n            std::vector<std::array<idx_t, 3>> newFaces;\n            std::map<std::pair<idx_t, idx_t>, idx_t> midpointCache;\n\n            auto getMidpoint = [&](idx_t i1, idx_t i2) -> idx_t {\n                auto key = std::make_pair(std::min(i1, i2), std::max(i1, i2));\n                auto it = midpointCache.find(key);\n                if (it != midpointCache.end()) return it->second;\n\n                Vec3 mid = (vertices[i1] + vertices[i2]) / 2.0f;\n                mid = mid.normalized() * radius;\n                idx_t idx = static_cast<idx_t>(vertices.size());\n                vertices.push_back(mid);\n                midpointCache[key] = idx;\n                return idx;\n            };\n\n            for (const auto& face : faces) {\n                idx_t a = getMidpoint(face[0], face[1]);\n                idx_t b = getMidpoint(face[1], face[2]);\n                idx_t c = getMidpoint(face[2], face[0]);\n\n                newFaces.push_back({face[0], a, c});\n                newFaces.push_back({face[1], b, a});\n                newFaces.push_back({face[2], c, b});\n                newFaces.push_back({a, b, c});\n            }\n            faces = std::move(newFaces);\n        }\n\n        // Build triangles (normals pointing inward for a \"room\")\n        triangles.reserve(faces.size());\n        for (const auto& face : faces) {\n            // Reverse winding to make normals point inward\n            triangles.emplace_back(vertices[face[2]], vertices[face[1]], vertices[face[0]]);\n        }\n    }\n};\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Random Number Generation\n// ============================================================================\n\nclass RandomGenerator {\n    std::mt19937 rng;\n    std::uniform_real_distribution<val_t> dist;\npublic:\n    explicit RandomGenerator(uint32_t seed = 42) : rng(seed), dist(0.0f, 1.0f) {}\n    val_t rand() { return dist(rng); }\n};\n\n// Generate a random point inside a triangle using barycentric coordinates\nVec3 randomPointInTriangle(const Triangle& t, RandomGenerator& rng) {\n    val_t u = rng.rand();\n    val_t v = rng.rand();\n    if (u + v > 1.0f) {\n        u = 1.0f - u;\n        v = 1.0f - v;\n    }\n    Vec3 ab = t.b - t.a;\n    Vec3 ac = t.c - t.a;\n    return t.a + ab * u + ac * v;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Ray-Triangle Intersection (Möller-Trumbore algorithm)\n// ============================================================================\n\nval_t rayTriangleIntersect(const Vec3& orig, const Vec3& dir,\n                            const Vec3& v0, const Vec3& v1, const Vec3& v2) {\n    Vec3 e1 = v1 - v0;\n    Vec3 e2 = v2 - v0;\n    Vec3 pvec = dir.cross(e2);\n    val_t det = e1.dot(pvec);\n\n    if (std::abs(det) < EPSILON) return std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n\n    val_t invDet = 1.0f / det;\n    Vec3 tvec = orig - v0;\n    val_t u = tvec.dot(pvec) * invDet;\n    if (u < 0.0f || u > 1.0f) return std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n\n    Vec3 qvec = tvec.cross(e1);\n    val_t v = dir.dot(qvec) * invDet;\n    if (v < 0.0f || u + v > 1.0f) return std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n\n    return e2.dot(qvec) * invDet;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Visibility Testing (Octree-accelerated)\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Check if a ray between two triangles is blocked by any other triangle\n// Uses octree for O(log N) instead of O(N) search\nbool isRayBlocked(const Vec3& from, const Vec3& to,\n                  const Octree& octree,\n                  size_t srcTriIdx, size_t dstTriIdx) {\n    Vec3 dir = to - from;\n    val_t rayLen = dir.norm();\n    if (rayLen < EPSILON) return true;\n    Vec3 dirNorm = dir / rayLen;\n\n    return octree.applyToTris(from, to, [&](size_t idx, const Triangle& tri) {\n        if (idx == srcTriIdx || idx == dstTriIdx) return false;\n\n        val_t dist = rayTriangleIntersect(from, dirNorm, tri.a, tri.b, tri.c);\n        if (dist > EPSILON && dist < rayLen - EPSILON) {\n            return true;  // Ray is blocked\n        }\n        return false;\n    });\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Form Factor Computation (Kij)\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Compute the cosine of angle between vector and triangle normal\nval_t cosPhi(const Vec3& v, const Vec3& normal) {\n    val_t vNorm = v.norm();\n    if (vNorm <= EPSILON) return ZERO;\n    return std::max(ZERO, v.dot(normal) / vNorm);\n}\n\n// Compute form factor Kij between triangle i (receiver) and triangle j (emitter)\nval_t computeKij(size_t idxI, size_t idxJ,\n                  const std::vector<Triangle>& triangles,\n                  const Octree& octree,\n                  RandomGenerator& rng) {\n    const Triangle& triI = triangles[idxI];\n    const Triangle& triJ = triangles[idxJ];\n\n    // Cull triangles facing the same direction\n    if (triI.normal().dot(triJ.normal()) > 0.99f) return ZERO;\n\n    val_t kij = ZERO;\n\n    for (int r = 0; r < NUM_RAYS; ++r) {\n        Vec3 pI = randomPointInTriangle(triI, rng);\n        Vec3 pJ = randomPointInTriangle(triJ, rng);\n\n        if (isRayBlocked(pI, pJ, octree, idxI, idxJ)) continue;\n\n        Vec3 v = pJ - pI;\n        val_t distSqr = v.squaredNorm();\n        if (distSqr < EPSILON) continue;\n\n        val_t cosPhiI = cosPhi(v, triI.normal());\n        val_t cosPhiJ = cosPhi(-v, triJ.normal());\n\n        if (cosPhiI <= ZERO || cosPhiJ <= ZERO) continue;\n\n        kij += (cosPhiI * cosPhiJ) / (PI * distSqr);\n    }\n\n    return kij * INV_NUM_RAYS;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Tau (time delay) Computation\n// ============================================================================\n\nint computeTau(const Triangle& triI, const Triangle& triJ) {\n    val_t dist = (triI.center() - triJ.center()).norm();\n    return static_cast<int>(std::ceil(dist * INV_WAVE_SPEED));\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Room Response Simulation State\n// ============================================================================\n\nstruct SimulationState {\n    size_t numTriangles;\n    size_t numTimesteps;\n\n    std::vector<Triangle> triangles;\n    std::vector<val_t> areas;       // Area of each triangle\n    std::vector<val_t> rho;         // Reflectivity (0.0 to 1.0)\n    std::vector<val_t> kij;         // Form factors (N x N matrix, row-major)\n    std::vector<int> tau;           // Time delays (N x N matrix, row-major)\n    std::vector<val_t> radE;        // Emission radiosity (T x N matrix)\n    std::vector<val_t> radB;        // Reflected radiosity (T x N matrix)\n    std::vector<val_t> distances;   // Computed distances from source\n\n    Octree octree;                  // Spatial acceleration structure\n\n    size_t sourceIndex;\n\n    size_t idx2d(size_t i, size_t j) const { return i * numTriangles + j; }\n    size_t idxTN(size_t t, size_t n) const { return t * numTriangles + n; }\n};\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Initialization\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid initializeSimulation(SimulationState& state, int subdivisions, size_t timesteps,\n                          size_t sourceIdx, val_t reflectivity) {\n    // Generate mesh\n    IcosphereMesh mesh(subdivisions, 10.0f);  // Radius 10 units\n    state.triangles = std::move(mesh.triangles);\n    state.numTriangles = state.triangles.size();\n    state.numTimesteps = timesteps;\n    state.sourceIndex = sourceIdx % state.numTriangles;\n\n    printf(\"Generated icosphere mesh with %zu triangles\\n\", state.numTriangles);\n\n    // Build octree for spatial acceleration\n    printf(\"Building octree...\\n\");\n    state.octree.build(state.triangles);\n\n    // Initialize areas\n    state.areas.resize(state.numTriangles);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n        state.areas[i] = state.triangles[i].area();\n    }\n\n    // Initialize reflectivity\n    state.rho.resize(state.numTriangles, reflectivity);\n\n    // Initialize matrices\n    state.kij.resize(state.numTriangles * state.numTriangles, ZERO);\n    state.tau.resize(state.numTriangles * state.numTriangles, 0);\n    state.radE.resize(timesteps * state.numTriangles, ZERO);\n    state.radB.resize(timesteps * state.numTriangles, ZERO);\n    state.distances.resize(state.numTriangles, ZERO);\n\n    // Set source emission (active for first half of timesteps)\n    size_t timeOn = 0;\n    size_t timeOff = timesteps / 2;\n    for (size_t t = timeOn; t < timeOff; ++t) {\n        state.radE[state.idxTN(t, state.sourceIndex)] = 1.0f;\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Precomputation Phase\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid computeFormFactors(SimulationState& state) {\n    printf(\"Computing form factors (Kij)...\\n\");\n    RandomGenerator rng(42);\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < state.numTriangles; ++j) {\n            if (i == j) continue;\n            state.kij[state.idx2d(i, j)] = computeKij(\n                i, j, state.triangles, state.octree, rng);\n        }\n        if ((i + 1) % 100 == 0 || i + 1 == state.numTriangles) {\n            printf(\"  Progress: %zu/%zu triangles\\n\", i + 1, state.numTriangles);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nvoid computeTimeDelays(SimulationState& state) {\n    printf(\"Computing time delays (Tau)...\\n\");\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < state.numTriangles; ++j) {\n            if (i == j) continue;\n            state.tau[state.idx2d(i, j)] = computeTau(\n                state.triangles[i], state.triangles[j]);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Simulation Phase (Wave Propagation)\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid runSimulation(SimulationState& state) {\n    printf(\"Running wave propagation simulation...\\n\");\n\n    for (size_t t = 0; t < state.numTimesteps; ++t) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n            val_t sumB = ZERO;\n\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < state.numTriangles; ++j) {\n                if (i == j) continue;\n\n                int tauij = state.tau[state.idx2d(i, j)];\n\n                // Skip if wave hasn't yet propagated from j to i\n                if (static_cast<int>(t) < tauij) continue;\n\n                val_t kij = state.kij[state.idx2d(i, j)];\n                if (kij <= ZERO) continue;\n\n                // Get radiosity from source triangle at time when emission occurred\n                size_t srcTime = t - static_cast<size_t>(tauij);\n                val_t radJ = state.radB[state.idxTN(srcTime, j)];\n                if (radJ <= ZERO) continue;\n\n                // Accumulate contribution: form factor * area * source radiosity\n                sumB += std::min(kij * state.areas[j], ONE) * radJ;\n            }\n\n state.numTimesteps) {\n            printf(\"  Timestep %zu/%zu\\n\", t + 1, state.numTimesteps);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Distance Computation (Cross-Correlation)\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid computeDistances(SimulationState& state) {\n    printf(\"Computing distances via cross-correlation...\\n\");\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n        val_t maxCorr = ZERO;\n        int bestT = 0;\n\n        // Discrete cross-correlation to find time delay\n        for (size_t t = 0; t < state.numTimesteps; ++t) {\n            val_t sum = ZERO;\n\n            for (size_t tt = t; tt < state.numTimesteps; ++tt) {\n                val_t pB = state.radB[state.idxTN(tt, i)];\n For the octree itself, I'm designing a flattened node structure with center, half-extent, child indices, and triangle range fields, then thinking through how to traverse the host-built recursive octree to populate this flat array while handling edge cases like leaf nodes with empty triangle lists.\n\nFor device-side traversal, leaf triangles get stored in a flat index array that points back into the global triangle buffer, and I'll copy the Triangle struct directly via cudaMemcpy since it's already simple data. I'm planning to write standalone HD helper functions for ray-box intersection rather than reusing host-only Octree methods, since the kernel will rely entirely on the flattened structure with no CPU fallback path.\n\nNow I should strip out the now-unused host-only functions like isRayBlocked and computeKij to keep things clean, and move the random-point-in-triangle logic to a device-compatible version since sampling happens inside the kernel while only the uniform random numbers are generated on the host. I'm working through the simulation kernel's time-stepping logic to make sure the radiosity accumulation—summing contributions from other triangles weighted by view factors and delayed by travel time—matches the original CPU version exactly, including the integer truncation of time values.\n\nI'm laying out the device memory layout: flattened view-factor and delay arrays indexed by column-major triangle pairs for coalesced access, area and reflectivity arrays per triangle, and a radiosity history buffer indexed by timestep and triangle. Emission is computed inline in the kernel as a simple on/off pulse from the source triangle rather than stored, and each rank's kernel writes its owned triangles' radiosity values directly into the shared device history buffer at the current timestep so they can be gathered across ranks afterward.\n\nNow I'm thinking through how to synchronize that history across ranks: the simplest approach is to keep a host-side mirror of the radiosity history, copy each rank's freshly computed local values down to host, use MPI_Allgather to assemble the full row across all ranks, then copy that assembled row back up to the device so all ranks have the complete history for the next step. This adds a small sync and copy cost per timestep but keeps things straightforward, and I'm deciding not to bother with multiple ranks sharing a single GPU for now.\n\nFor distances, since N×T² works out to only about 50 million operations, it's cheap enough that each rank can just compute distances for its owned indices with OpenMP and then Allgather, reusing the same helper pattern as the radiosity history gather rather than overcomplicating things. Validation counts like received energy and non-zero kij can be handled similarly, with a device-side count kernel per rank reduced to the root via MPI_Reduce.\n\nNow I'm sketching the host-side layout for computeFormFactors: tracking N, T, P, rank, and the per-rank row count L, while making sure things degrade gracefully when P exceeds N and some ranks end up with zero owned rows.\n\nI'm defining the culling check that compares triangle normals via dot product and treats near-parallel triangles (dot > 0.99) as culled, returning zero form factor in that case. Then I need per-row counts of non-culled pairs across all N rows, computed with an OpenMP parallel loop — even at N=20480 this is a few hundred million dot products, fast enough with threading, and it's fine that every rank redundantly computes it.\n\nI'm sketching out the RNG stream logic: each row consumes a fixed number of draws, so the starting position for row i is determined by a prefix sum of draw counts, and generation proceeds in rounds processing windows of rows across ranks in sequence.\n\nI'm working out the indexing so that within each round, a rank's locally owned row maps to a slot index via dividing the offset from the window start by the number of ranks, confirming the modular arithmetic lines up correctly. For owned rows, I generate and store four floats per non-culled pair in a fixed order, while for non-owned rows I just discard the appropriate number of draws — though I need to double check how the random engine's discard count relates to the number of actual values generated, since library-specific generation routines can consume a variable number of underlying engine calls per value.\n\nConfirming that for this float/precision combination the engine consumes exactly one call per draw, so the discard count scales cleanly with the number of draws, and that the ordering across rows within a round stays consistent regardless of ownership. Now I'm shifting to the device-side per-round buffer setup.\n\nI'm laying out the row-id and uniform buffers alongside the kernel that computes each thread's row pair, maps global indices to local round slots, handles culled or diagonal entries by writing explicit zeros, and stores the resulting value into the transposed kij array—followed by the per-pair ray evaluation loop that comes next.\n\nChecking the ray-blocking logic: degenerate rays count as blocked, and I'm using FLT_MAX from cfloat as the \"no intersection\" sentinel since it's safely usable in device code without constexpr concerns.\n\nI'm writing the flat octree traversal for shadow ray blocking tests using an explicit stack instead of recursion, pushing child nodes after box-hit checks and scanning leaf triangles for intersections while skipping the source and destination triangle indices. I'm making sure the root node is handled the same way as the original recursive version—pushed without an initial box test—and double-checking that each flattened node still carries its own center and half-extent for child box tests.\n\nNow I'm working out how deep the octree can actually get so I can size the fixed-size stack array correctly: since each split roughly halves the box size and leaves stop splitting once their extent drops below 0.5, the max depth should land around 7-9 levels, giving a worst-case stack occupancy of roughly 7*depth+1. I'm leaning toward a stack size of 64 with a host-side depth check to guarantee it's never exceeded, weighing that against per-thread local memory cost for a 128-thread block.\n\nI also need to keep the host-side Octree class but strip out the box-intersection and triangle-application logic, replacing it with a free HD function, and add a flatten step for the GPU representation — the build process still owns the triangle pointers. For the time-delay kernel, I'm converting the host computeTau function (which measures distance between triangle centroids and divides by wave speed, rounding up) into a device-compatible version using ceilf, then mapping each thread to a (j, li) pair to compute and write into the tau table.\n\nI'm reordering the thread-to-index mapping so writes to the tau and kij tables are coalesced — choosing p = j*L + li (or j*K + s for the form factor kernel) so adjacent threads write adjacent memory, since consecutive slots correspond to consecutive row indices within a scheduling round. The ray-tracing loop dominates runtime anyway, so I'm keeping the layout simple rather than over-optimizing memory access patterns.\n\nRather than passing explicit row-id arrays, I'll just pass windowStart, rank, P, K, N as kernel parameters and compute each row index directly as i = windowStart + rank + P*s, checking validity against N inside the kernel.\n\nNow I'm designing the kernel signature and launch scheme: it takes the triangle/node/leaf arrays, the uniform buffer, and output buffer along with N, K, P, rank, window size and length, with each thread using a small local stack for traversal. For pipelining, I'm setting up double-buffered pinned host and device memory with separate streams per round, carefully syncing each buffer's stream before it's reused or overwritten — generating uniforms into a host buffer, copying asynchronously to device, launching the kernel, and syncing the previous round's stream before advancing.\n\nI'm then estimating the generation cost: for each round, roughly 15.7M draws take about 31ms per rank, but since each rank discards draws not belonging to it, the aggregate discard cost across all P ranks roughly matches the full generation cost, meaning throughput scales unfavorably with rank count.\n\nOn the GPU side, I'm roughly sizing kernel time against host generation time—for a single GPU, the traversal work across roughly 245k thread-pairs dominates at around 0.25s per round, so host-side generation stays comfortably hidden. For multi-rank setups across 2 GPUs, I'm planning to just assign devices round-robin via cudaSetDevice based on rank modulo device count, and I'll rely on actual measurement rather than further estimation to confirm the balance holds.\n\nI'm also mapping out where OpenMP parallelism actually matters: culling counts and distance computations over owned rows are good parallel-for candidates, while RNG discarding, octree flattening, and mesh generation stay serial since they're inherently sequential. For most problem sizes this is trivial overhead, but I'm checking whether host-side generation could ever dominate at large N—estimating that for N=5120, the total RNG draw count comes out to roughly 1.7 billion draws, translating to a few seconds of serial generation per rank, which could become a real bottleneck worth watching.\n\nChecking N=20480 gives a serial floor around 54 seconds per rank from draws alone, while the GPU-side work handling hundreds of millions of ray pairs likely takes tens of minutes—so the CPU floor stays proportionally small and acceptable.\n\nNow I'm designing the GPU simulation kernel itself: for each owned row index, I loop over all other elements, skip self-pairs and zero-visibility or zero-radiosity sources, respect time-of-flight delays by indexing into the radiosity history buffer at the appropriate past timestep, accumulate clamped view-factor-weighted contributions, and add a source emission term during the active emission window.\n\nI need to disable FMA contraction (--fmad=false) so sumB accumulation matches the original scalar math exactly. For history management, I'll assemble each timestep's full radiosity row on the host after the allgather and copy it to the device in one shot, rather than having the kernel write its own entries directly to device memory—dropping that redundant write since there's no read-after-write hazard within the same timestep.\n\nFor distances, each rank computes its owned rows using the full host radB history (already synced across ranks), then an allgather assembles the full distances array everywhere so any rank can hash/validate/print results.\n\nFor validation, I still need the per-row correlation maxima, the nonzero kij count reduced across ranks via MPI_Reduce (possibly from a device atomic counter), and the usual percentage/triangle totals, with only the root printing and broadcasting the pass/fail result so all ranks exit consistently.\n\nI'll have root compute the hash and print results, using MPI_Barrier-wrapped timers around time delays, form factors, simulation, and distance computation phases to match the original's progress messages, while octree/mesh setup stays untimed as before.\n\nSince all ranks parse the same argv, I need to guard option-parsing errors and the -h usage print so only rank 0 outputs them, calling MPI_Finalize before any early exit. For numeric consistency between host and device, I'm keeping the same float arithmetic order for wave speed and distance calculations on both sides so results match exactly.\n\nI'm also checking that normal vectors computed on the host constructor get copied correctly to device-side triangle data, and that the normalize helper handles near-zero vectors safely. To guarantee identical IEEE floating-point results between host and device, I'm disabling fused multiply-add and contraction on both compilers — passing `-ffp-contract=off` to the host compiler through nvcc's `-Xcompiler` flag and `--fmad=false` for device code, configured via CMake's CUDA compile options.\n\nI should test whether GCC's default FMA contraction actually changes the hash output on the original baseline (since GNU dialect defaults to fast contraction with `-march=native`), running this comparison at a small N first and then at a larger N to confirm. I also want to verify the octree's ray traversal and box-intersection logic stay untouched while removing unused methods from the class.\n\nWriting the flattening function...\n\nI'm double-checking that vector reallocation doesn't break anything since I'm using indices rather than raw pointers, and confirming the leaf-detection logic and root handling match the original octree semantics. ++k) {\n                const uint32_t idx = leafTris[nd.triBegin + k];\n                if (idx == srcIdx || idx == dstIdx) continue;\n                const Triangle& tri = tris[idx];\n                val_t dist = rayTriangleIntersect(from, dirNorm, tri.a, tri.b, tri.c);\n                if (dist > EPSILON && dist < rayLen - EPSILON) {\n                    return true;\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            for (int c = 0; c < 8; ++c) {\n                const int32_t ci = nd.child[c];\n                if (ci >= 0 && rayIntersectsBox(nodes[ci].center, nodes[ci].halfExtent, from, to)) {\n                    stack[sp++] = ci;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return false;\n}\n\n// Cosine between vector and triangle normal, clamped at zero\nHD inline val_t cosPhi(const Vec3& v, const Vec3& normal) {\n    val_t vNorm = v.norm();\n    if (vNorm <= EPSILON) return ZERO;\n    return hmax(ZERO, v.dot(normal) / vNorm);\n}\n\n// Culling test: triangles facing the same direction exchange no energy\nHD inline bool isCulled(const Triangle& triI, const Triangle& triJ) {\n    return triI.normal().dot(triJ.normal()) > 0.99f;\n}\n\n// Form factor Kij for receiver i and emitter j given the 64 uniform samples\n// consumed in the order (uI, vI, uJ, vJ) per ray.\nHD inline val_t computeKij(uint32_t i, uint32_t j, const Triangle* tris,\n                           const FlatNode* nodes, const uint32_t* leafTris,\n                           const float* uu) {\n    const Triangle& triI = tris[i];\n    const Triangle& triJ = tris[j];\n\n    if (isCulled(triI, triJ)) return ZERO;\n\n    val_t kij = ZERO;\n\n    for (int r = 0; r < NUM_RAYS; ++r) {\n        const float* q = uu + r * 4;\n        Vec3 pI = pointInTriangle(triI, q[0], q[1]);\n        Vec3 pJ = pointInTriangle(triJ, q[2], q[3]);\n\n        if (isRayBlocked(pI, pJ, nodes, leafTris, tris, i, j)) continue;\n\n        Vec3 v = pJ - pI;\n        val_t distSqr = v.squaredNorm();\n        if (distSqr < EPSILON) continue;\n\n        val_t cosPhiI = cosPhi(v, triI.normal());\n        val_t cosPhiJ = cosPhi(-v, triJ.normal());\n\n        if (cosPhiI <= ZERO || cosPhiJ <= ZERO) continue;\n\n        kij += (cosPhiI * cosPhiJ) / (PI * distSqr);\n    }\n\n    return kij * INV_NUM_RAYS;\n}\n\n// Time delay in simulation steps between two triangle centers\nHD inline int computeTau(const Triangle& triI, const Triangle& triJ) {\n    val_t dist = (triI.center() - triJ.center()).norm();\n    return static_cast<int>(ceilf(dist * INV_WAVE_SPEED));\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// CUDA Kernels\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Tau for the owned receiver rows, stored as tauT[j * L + li] (coalesced in li).\n__global__ void timeDelayKernel(const Triangle* tris, int* tauT,\n                                uint32_t N, uint32_t L, uint32_t P, uint32_t rank) {\n    const size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (p >= static_cast<size_t>(N) * L) return;\n    const uint32_t j = static_cast<uint32_t>(p / L);\n    const uint32_t li = static_cast<uint32_t>(p % L);\n    const uint32_t i = rank + P * li;\n    tauT[p] = (i == j) ? 0 : computeTau(tris[i], tris[j]);\n}\n\n// Form factors for one round of owned rows. Thread p maps to (j, slot s) with\n// p = j * K + s; the uniform samples for that pair start at uni[p * 64].\n__global__ void formFactorKernel(const Triangle* tris, const FlatNode* nodes,\n                                 const uint32_t* leafTris, const float* uni,\n                                 float* kijT, uint32_t N, uint32_t L, uint32_t P,\n                                 uint32_t rank, uint32_t K, uint32_t windowStart) {\n    const size_t p = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (p >= static_cast<size_t>(N) * K) return;\n    const uint32_t j = static_cast<uint32_t>(p / K);\n    const uint32_t s = static_cast<uint32_t>(p % K);\n    const uint32_t i = windowStart + rank + P * s;\n    if (i >= N || i == j) return;\n\n    const uint32_t li = (i - rank) / P;\n    const float* uu = uni + p * 64;\n    kijT[static_cast<size_t>(j) * L + li] =\n        computeKij(i, j, tris, nodes, leafTris, uu);\n}\n\n// One wave-propagation timestep for the owned receivers. Each thread sums over j\n// in ascending order exactly as the sequential algorithm does.\n__global__ void simulateKernel(const float* kijT, const int* tauT, const float* areas,\n                               const float* rho, const float* radB, float* outLocal,\n                               uint32_t t, uint32_t N, uint32_t L, uint32_t P,\n                               uint32_t rank, uint32_t timeOff, uint32_t source) {\n    const uint32_t li = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (li >= L) return;\n    const uint32_t i = rank + P * li;\n\n    val_t sumB = ZERO;\n    for (uint32_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n        if (j == i) continue;\n\n        const size_t off = static_cast<size_t>(j) * L + li;\n        const int tauij = tauT[off];\n\n        // Skip if wave hasn't yet propagated from j to i\n        if (static_cast<int>(t) < tauij) continue;\n\n        const val_t kij = kijT[off];\n        if (kij <= ZERO) continue;\n\n        // Radiosity emitted by j at the time the wave left it\n        const size_t srcTime = static_cast<size_t>(t) - static_cast<size_t>(tauij);\n        const val_t radJ = radB[srcTime * N + j];\n        if (radJ <= ZERO) continue;\n\n        sumB += hmin(kij * areas[j], ONE) * radJ;\n    }\n\n    const val_t radE = (t < timeOff && i == source) ? ONE : ZERO;\n    outLocal[li] = rho[i] * sumB + radE;\n}\n\n// Count entries above EPSILON (validation only)\n__global__ void countNonZeroKernel(const float* kijT, size_t n, unsigned long long* count) {\n    const size_t idx = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (idx < n && kijT[idx] > EPSILON) {\n        atomicAdd(count, 1ULL);\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Simulation State\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Number of receiver rows owned by 'rank' in the cyclic distribution i = rank + P*li\nstatic size_t ownedCount(size_t N, size_t rank, size_t P) {\n    return rank < N ? (N - rank - 1) / P + 1 : 0;\n}\n\nstruct DeviceData {\n    Triangle* tris = nullptr;\n    FlatNode* nodes = nullptr;\n    uint32_t* leafTris = nullptr;\n    float* areas = nullptr;\n    float* rho = nullptr;\n    float* kijT = nullptr;      // [j * L + li]\n    int* tauT = nullptr;        // [j * L + li]\n    float* radB = nullptr;      // [t * N + i], full history\n    float* outLocal = nullptr;  // [li] values of the current timestep\n    float* uni[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};        // round sample buffers (device)\n    float* hostUni[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};    // round sample buffers (pinned host)\n    cudaStream_t streams[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};\n    unsigned long long* counter = nullptr;\n};\n\nstruct SimulationState {\n    size_t numTriangles = 0;\n    size_t numTimesteps = 0;\n    size_t sourceIndex = 0;\n    size_t numOwned = 0;      // receiver rows owned by this rank\n    size_t numOwnedMax = 0;   // ceil(N / P): padded per-rank slot count\n\n    std::vector<Triangle> triangles;\n    std::vector<val_t> areas;       // Area of each triangle\n    std::vector<val_t> rho;         // Reflectivity (0.0 to 1.0)\n    std::vector<val_t> radB;        // Radiosity history (T x N), replicated on all ranks\n    std::vector<val_t> distances;   // Computed distances from source (N), replicated\n\n    FlatOctree octree;              // Spatial acceleration structure\n    DeviceData dev;\n};\n\n// Gather one value per owned row from every rank into a full N-length array.\n// 'local' must hold numOwnedMax entries (padding unused).\nstatic void allgatherOwnedRows(const std::vector<val_t>& local, size_t N, val_t* full) {\n    const size_t P = static_cast<size_t>(gSize);\n    const size_t Lmax = (N + P - 1) / P;\n    std::vector<val_t> recv(P * Lmax);\n    MPI_Allgather(local.data(), static_cast<int>(Lmax), MPI_FLOAT,\n                  recv.data(), static_cast<int>(Lmax), MPI_FLOAT, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    for (size_t r = 0; r < P; ++r) {\n        const size_t cnt = ownedCount(N, r, P);\n        for (size_t li = 0; li < cnt; ++li) {\n            full[r + P * li] = recv[r * Lmax + li];\n        }\n    }\n}\n\ntemplate <typename T>\nstatic T* deviceAlloc(size_t count) {\n    T* p = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&p, std::max<size_t>(count, 1) * sizeof(T)));\n    return p;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Initialization\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid initializeSimulation(SimulationState& state, int subdivisions, size_t timesteps,\n                          size_t sourceIdx, val_t reflectivity) {\n    // Generate mesh\n    IcosphereMesh mesh(subdivisions, 10.0f);  // Radius 10 units\n    state.triangles = std::move(mesh.triangles);\n    state.numTriangles = state.triangles.size();\n    state.numTimesteps = timesteps;\n    state.sourceIndex = sourceIdx % state.numTriangles;\n\n    const size_t N = state.numTriangles;\n    const size_t P = static_cast<size_t>(gSize);\n    state.numOwned = ownedCount(N, static_cast<size_t>(gRank), P);\n    state.numOwnedMax = (N + P - 1) / P;\n\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Generated icosphere mesh with %zu triangles\\n\", state.numTriangles);\n\n    // Build octree for spatial acceleration and flatten it for the device\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Building octree...\\n\");\n    {\n        Octree octree;\n        octree.build(state.triangles);\n        flattenNode(octree, state.octree, 0);\n    }\n    if (7 * state.octree.maxDepth + 1 > TRAVERSAL_STACK) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"Octree too deep (%d levels) for traversal stack\\n\", state.octree.maxDepth);\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n\n    // Initialize areas\n    state.areas.resize(N);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        state.areas[i] = state.triangles[i].area();\n    }\n\n    // Initialize reflectivity\n    state.rho.assign(N, reflectivity);\n\n    // Radiosity history and distances\n    state.radB.assign(timesteps * N, ZERO);\n    state.distances.assign(N, ZERO);\n}\n\n// Select the GPU, allocate device data and upload the static problem description.\nvoid setupDevice(SimulationState& state) {\n    int numDevices = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&numDevices));\n    if (numDevices == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"roomsim requires a CUDA device, none found\\n\");\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(gLocalRank % numDevices));\n\n    const size_t N = state.numTriangles;\n    const size_t L = state.numOwned;\n    const size_t T = state.numTimesteps;\n    DeviceData& d = state.dev;\n\n    d.tris = deviceAlloc<Triangle>(N);\n    d.nodes = deviceAlloc<FlatNode>(state.octree.nodes.size());\n    d.leafTris = deviceAlloc<uint32_t>(state.octree.leafTris.size());\n    d.areas = deviceAlloc<float>(N);\n    d.rho = deviceAlloc<float>(N);\n    d.kijT = deviceAlloc<float>(N * L);\n    d.tauT = deviceAlloc<int>(N * L);\n    d.radB = deviceAlloc<float>(T * N);\n    d.outLocal = deviceAlloc<float>(state.numOwnedMax);\n    d.counter = deviceAlloc<unsigned long long>(1);\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d.tris, state.triangles.data(), N * sizeof(Triangle), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d.nodes, state.octree.nodes.data(),\n                          state.octree.nodes.size() * sizeof(FlatNode), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d.leafTris, state.octree.leafTris.data(),\n                          state.octree.leafTris.size() * sizeof(uint32_t), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d.areas, state.areas.data(), N * sizeof(float), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d.rho, state.rho.data(), N * sizeof(float), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemset(d.kijT, 0, std::max<size_t>(N * L, 1) * sizeof(float)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemset(d.radB, 0, std::max<size_t>(T * N, 1) * sizeof(float)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemset(d.counter, 0, sizeof(unsigned long long)));\n\n    for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamCreate(&d.streams[k]));\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Precomputation Phase\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid computeTimeDelays(SimulationState& state) {\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Computing time delays (Tau)...\\n\");\n    const size_t N = state.numTriangles;\n    const size_t L = state.numOwned;\n    if (N * L > 0) {\n        const size_t total = N * L;\n        const unsigned blocks = static_cast<unsigned>((total + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE);\n        timeDelayKernel<<<blocks, BLOCK_SIZE>>>(state.dev.tris, state.dev.tauT,\n                                                 static_cast<uint32_t>(N), static_cast<uint32_t>(L),\n                                                 static_cast<uint32_t>(gSize), static_cast<uint32_t>(gRank));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n    }\n}\n\nvoid computeFormFactors(SimulationState& state) {\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Computing form factors (Kij)...\\n\");\n\n    const size_t N = state.numTriangles;\n    const size_t L = state.numOwned;\n    const size_t P = static_cast<size_t>(gSize);\n    const size_t R = static_cast<size_t>(gRank);\n    DeviceData& d = state.dev;\n\n    // The sampling stream of the sequential algorithm advances 64 draws for every\n    // non-culled pair (i, j), i != j. Count those per receiver so that each rank can\n    // skip over rows it does not own without generating their samples.\n    std::vector<uint64_t> partners(N);\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (long i = 0; i < static_cast<long>(N); ++i) {\n        uint64_t c = 0;\n        const Triangle& ti = state.triangles[i];\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            if (j != static_cast<size_t>(i) && !isCulled(ti, state.triangles[j])) ++c;\n        }\n        partners[i] = c;\n    }\n\n    // Rows are processed in rounds. A round covers a window of P*K consecutive\n    // global rows; rank r handles the K rows congruent to r modulo P in that window.\n    const size_t K = std::min<size_t>(std::max<size_t>(1, (size_t{1} << 18) / N), (N + P - 1) / P);\n    const size_t window = K * P;\n    const size_t numRounds = (N + window - 1) / window;\n    const size_t bufFloats = N * K * 64;\n\n    for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMallocHost(&d.hostUni[k], bufFloats * sizeof(float)));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d.uni[k], bufFloats * sizeof(float)));\n    }\n\n    RandomGenerator rng(42);\n\n    // Fill the host sample buffer for round g in the exact stream order.\n    // Layout: buf[(j * K + s) * 64 + r * 4 + q] with q = (uI, vI, uJ, vJ).\n    auto generateRound = [&](size_t g, float* buf) {\n        const size_t W = g * window;\n        const size_t end = std::min(N, W + window);\n        for (size_t i = W; i < end; ++i) {\n            if (i % P != R) {\n                rng.skip(64ULL * partners[i]);\n                continue;\n            }\n            const size_t s = (i - W) / P;\n            const Triangle& ti = state.triangles[i];\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n                if (j == i || isCulled(ti, state.triangles[j])) continue;\n                float* dst = buf + (j * K + s) * 64;\n                for (int q = 0; q < 64; ++q) dst[q] = rng.rand();\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    size_t doneBefore = 0;\n    generateRound(0, d.hostUni[0]);\n    for (size_t g = 0; g < numRounds; ++g) {\n        const int k = static_cast<int>(g & 1);\n        const size_t W = g * window;\n        const size_t done = std::min(N, W + window);\n\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(d.uni[k], d.hostUni[k], bufFloats * sizeof(float),\n                                   cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, d.streams[k]));\n\n        const size_t total = N * K;\n        const unsigned blocks = static_cast<unsigned>((total + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE);\n        formFactorKernel<<<blocks, BLOCK_SIZE, 0, d.streams[k]>>>(\n            d.tris, d.nodes, d.leafTris, d.uni[k], d.kijT,\n            static_cast<uint32_t>(N), static_cast<uint32_t>(L), static_cast<uint32_t>(P),\n            static_cast<uint32_t>(R), static_cast<uint32_t>(K), static_cast<uint32_t>(W));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n        // Overlap: generate the next round's samples while this round runs on the GPU.\n        if (g + 1 < numRounds) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(d.streams[k ^ 1]));\n            generateRound(g + 1, d.hostUni[k ^ 1]);\n        }\n\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(d.streams[k]));\n        MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n        // Progress reporting in the same form as the sequential code\n        size_t mark = 100 * (doneBefore / 100 + 1);\n        for (; mark <= done; mark += 100) {\n            ROOT_PRINTF(\"  Progress: %zu/%zu triangles\\n\", mark, N);\n        }\n        if (done == N && N % 100 != 0) {\n            ROOT_PRINTF(\"  Progress: %zu/%zu triangles\\n\", N, N);\n        }\n        doneBefore = done;\n    }\n\n    for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFreeHost(d.hostUni[k]));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(d.uni[k]));\n        d.hostUni[k] = nullptr;\n        d.uni[k] = nullptr;\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Simulation Phase (Wave Propagation)\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid runSimulation(SimulationState& state) {\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Running wave propagation simulation...\\n\");\n\n    const size_t N = state.numTriangles;\n    const size_t T = state.numTimesteps;\n    const size_t L = state.numOwned;\n    const size_t P = static_cast<size_t>(gSize);\n    const size_t R = static_cast<size_t>(gRank);\n    DeviceData& d = state.dev;\n\n    std::vector<val_t> owned(state.numOwnedMax, ZERO);\n    const uint32_t timeOff = static_cast<uint32_t>(T / 2);  // source emits for the first half\n\n    for (size_t t = 0; t < T; ++t) {\n        if (L > 0) {\n            const unsigned blocks = static_cast<unsigned>((L + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE);\n            simulateKernel<<<blocks, BLOCK_SIZE>>>(\n                d.kijT, d.tauT, d.areas, d.rho, d.radB, d.outLocal,\n                static_cast<uint32_t>(t), static_cast<uint32_t>(N), static_cast<uint32_t>(L),\n                static_cast<uint32_t>(P), static_cast<uint32_t>(R), timeOff,\n                static_cast<uint32_t>(state.sourceIndex));\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(owned.data(), d.outLocal, L * sizeof(float), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        }\n\n        // Share this step's radiosity with all ranks\n        allgatherOwnedRows(owned, N, state.radB.data() + t * N);\n\n        // Update the device-resident history row for the next steps' delayed reads\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d.radB + t * N, state.radB.data() + t * N,\n                              N * sizeof(float), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n        if ((t + 1) % 10 == 0 || t + 1 == T) {\n            ROOT_PRINTF(\"  Timestep %zu/%zu\\n\", t + 1, T);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Copy the form factors back to the host only where validation needs them:\n// counts non-zero Kij entries across all ranks.\nunsigned long long countNonZeroKij(SimulationState& state) {\n    const size_t n = state.numTriangles * state.numOwned;\n    DeviceData& d = state.dev;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemset(d.counter, 0, sizeof(unsigned long long)));\n    if (n > 0) {\n        const unsigned blocks = static_cast<unsigned>((n + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE);\n        countNonZeroKernel<<<blocks, BLOCK_SIZE>>>(d.kijT, n, d.counter);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    }\n    unsigned long long local = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(&local, d.counter, sizeof(unsigned long long), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    unsigned long long total = 0;\n    MPI_Allreduce(&local, &total, 1, MPI_UNSIGNED_LONG_LONG, MPI_SUM, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    return total;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Distance Computation (Cross-Correlation)\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid computeDistances(SimulationState& state) {\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"Computing distances via cross-correlation...\\n\");\n\n    const size_t N = state.numTriangles;\n    const size_t T = state.numTimesteps;\n    const size_t L = state.numOwned;\n    const size_t P = static_cast<size_t>(gSize);\n    const size_t R = static_cast<size_t>(gRank);\n    const size_t src = state.sourceIndex;\n    const val_t* radB = state.radB.data();\n\n    std::vector<val_t> owned(state.numOwnedMax, ZERO);\n\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 4)\n    for (long li = 0; li < static_cast<long>(L); ++li) {\n        const size_t i = R + P * static_cast<size_t>(li);\n        val_t maxCorr = ZERO;\n        int bestT = 0;\n\n        // Discrete cross-correlation to find time delay\n        for (size_t t = 0; t < T; ++t) {\n            val_t sum = ZERO;\n\n            for (size_t tt = t; tt < T; ++tt) {\n                val_t pB = radB[tt * N + i];\n                val_t pS = radB[(tt - t) * N + src];\n                sum += pS * pB;\n            }\n\n            if (sum > maxCorr) {\n                maxCorr = sum;\n                bestT = static_cast<int>(t);\n            }\n        }\n\n        owned[li] = WAVE_SPEED * static_cast<val_t>(bestT);\n    }\n\n    allgatherOwnedRows(owned, N, state.distances.data());\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Validation\n// ============================================================================\n\nbool validateResults(const SimulationState& state, unsigned long long nonZeroKijTotal) {\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"\\nValidation:\\n\");\n\n    const size_t N = state.numTriangles;\n    const size_t T = state.numTimesteps;\n\n    // Check that distances are non-negative\n    bool allNonNegative = true;\n    val_t minDist = std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n    val_t maxDist = std::numeric_limits<val_t>::lowest();\n    val_t sumDist = ZERO;\n    int nonZeroCount = 0;\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        val_t d = state.distances[i];\n        if (d < 0) {\n            allNonNegative = false;\n            ROOT_PRINTF(\"  ERROR: Negative distance at triangle %zu: %f\\n\", i, d);\n        }\n        if (!std::isfinite(d)) {\n            ROOT_PRINTF(\"  ERROR: Non-finite distance at triangle %zu: %f\\n\", i, d);\n            return false;\n        }\n        minDist = std::min(minDist, d);\n        maxDist = std::max(maxDist, d);\n        sumDist += d;\n        if (d > EPSILON) nonZeroCount++;\n    }\n\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"  Distance range: [%.4f, %.4f]\\n\", minDist, maxDist);\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"  Average distance: %.4f\\n\", sumDist / static_cast<val_t>(N));\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"  Non-zero distances: %d/%zu\\n\", nonZeroCount, N);\n\n    // Check source distance is zero or very small\n    val_t srcDist = state.distances[state.sourceIndex];\n    if (srcDist > WAVE_SPEED * 2) {\n        ROOT_PRINTF(\"  WARNING: Source triangle distance is non-zero: %.4f\\n\", srcDist);\n    }\n\n    // Check radiosity propagation (some triangles should have received energy)\n    int receivedEnergy = 0;\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        for (size_t t = 0; t < T; ++t) {\n            if (state.radB[t * N + i] > EPSILON) {\n                receivedEnergy++;\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    ROOT_PRINTF(\"  Triangles {"type":"step_start","timestamp":1793151813013,"sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","part":{"id":"prt_1802d458f001YpGbC9aWTRIWk8","messageID":"msg_1802d3f5d0011dT70i9DVO5xk3","sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793151824041,"sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","part":{"id":"prt_1802d4592001ihd10Npe4ylPRK","messageID":"msg_1802d3f5d0011dT70i9DVO5xk3","sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","type":"reasoning","text":"It runs in 65 seconds for precomputation, and I suspect the serial RNG draws are the dominant cost: with N=20480 needing roughly 2.7e10 draws at about 2ns each, that alone accounts for nearly the full runtime, meaning GPU compute is likely overlapped and not the bottleneck. So the RNG generation floor seems to be what's limiting performance for large N, and I should look at ways to speed that up.\n\nThe twist operation that updates the Mersenne Twister state is the real cost, not the tempering, and it's inherently sequential since each state depends on the previous one—jump-ahead polynomial methods could parallelize this but add significant complexity. Parallelizing across ranks or generating the stream once without a jump-ahead approach isn't really feasible either, so I'm stuck without a faster skip mechanism unless libstdc++'s unvectorized generation loop itself can be optimized.\n\nGiven 65s for N=20480 versus an estimated many-hour baseline, this is still a massive speedup, but the RNG serial floor doesn't shrink with more GPUs, which caps strong scaling. Giving each rank a pre-skipped stream from a single serial pass wouldn't help since the ranks already run concurrently—so true jump-ahead math, computing x^k mod the characteristic polynomial over GF(2), seems like the only path to actually reduce that floor.\n\nI could try deriving the characteristic polynomial via Berlekamp-Massey at startup and using it for offset state computation, but that's a complex, error-prone implementation for maybe only a 60-second gain—so I'm weighing whether it's worth the risk versus just leveraging the recurrence structure directly to skip ahead more cheaply.\n\nRather than building the full jump-ahead machinery, I should first measure where the actual time is going—is discard() really the bottleneck, or is GPU work dominating the 65s? {"type":"step_start","timestamp":1793152216240,"sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","part":{"id":"prt_180336ca50016QGSy9edbqWeFt","messageID":"msg_18033673d001b0fPyW0fXgKFqm","sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793152237129,"sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","part":{"id":"prt_180336cad001XYGnoMHQXxO7s6","messageID":"msg_18033673d001b0fPyW0fXgKFqm","sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","type":"reasoning","text":"The GPU kernel dominates with about 21.9 seconds of GPU time for a single rank, while total precomputation under profiling runs around 45 seconds including overhead. I'm noticing cudaFreeHost calls taking 29 seconds each, which suggests they're blocking while waiting for the GPU to finish rather than being a genuine cost themselves.\n\nActually, re-reading the numbers more carefully, I realize I misread the cudaHostAlloc figure — it's 145 milliseconds total across two calls, not 72 seconds, which makes much more sense for allocating 63MB of pinned memory.\n\nSo the real breakdown is that GPU kernel time totals ~22 seconds while host-side work accounts for the rest: the serial RNG discard pass takes about 9 seconds, and the remaining time comes from parallel generation and memory transfers, with 1707 rounds matching N divided by block size 12 for the single-rank case.\n\nFor the 21.9s GPU kernel with N=20480, that translates to roughly 4.2e8 pairs times 16 rays each, landing around 3.3 microseconds per ray or 52ns per pair -- plausible for a 3090 with 10496 cores given the compute involved. I'm thinking about optimization angles: better octree traversal, shared memory usage, reducing warp divergence, though fast-math is off-limits since we need exactness. The thread indexing scheme (warp = same emitter j, different receiver rows i) should give good memory coherence since neighboring triangles on the icosphere are spatially close, so rays within a warp likely follow similar traversal paths through the structure.\n\nTriangle data loads are small (36-48 bytes) so cache behavior should be fine there. The real insight is that since isRayBlocked just needs to find whether any blocking triangle exists, any conservative traversal structure (BVH, different octree config, etc.) that doesn't produce false negatives will give an identical boolean result -- so the acceleration structure itself is free to change as long as it never misses a triangle the brute-force check would find.\n\nBut I realize the original octree is the reference semantics, including its own floating-point edge cases, so swapping structures risks subtly different results and hash mismatches -- better to keep the original octree and look for micro-optimizations: using `__restrict__`/`__ldg` for read-only data, and reconsidering whether octree nodes could live in shared memory. Given node counts are too large for shared memory, I'll keep them in global memory via the read-only cache path, and estimating the ideal FLOP count versus actual runtime suggests we're roughly 20x slower than ideal, likely due to warp divergence and local memory stack overhead.\n\nThat local memory traversal stack, sized dynamically and placed in local memory because of the compiler's indexing behavior, is probably the real bottleneck -- I'm weighing whether to shrink the stack size based on actual max depth rather than a worst-case bound, since accesses through L1 are moderate but not negligible. Still, given we've already achieved roughly 100x speedup over the original implementation and scale well to larger N, I think a light optimization pass focused on trimming unnecessary serial overhead is the most worthwhile next step rather than a deep restructuring.\n\nActually, the bigger win is overlapping the serial skip phase with GPU work: instead of running pass 1 fully up front, I can advance the random generator stream incrementally within the round loop, snapshotting only the rows needed for the next round's window before each round starts. That gives roughly 853 × 12.8ms ≈ 11s of kernel time per rank, plus H2D transfer overhead for the 63MB buffer each round—so I need to account for that extra transfer time to explain the discrepancy with the observed 28s.\n\nSince the H2D copy and kernel execution are sequential within a stream, the per-round time is closer to their sum rather than fully overlapped, which adds up across all rounds. One fix would be moving uniform generation onto the GPU itself, though generating mt19937 draws per row sequentially on-device seems too slow given the sheer volume of draws needed per thread.\n\nInstead, I'm restructuring the loop so the H2D transfer for the next round runs on a separate stream concurrently with the current kernel, using a copy engine to overlap transfer and compute properly rather than serializing them.\n\nActually since kernel g+1 is launched on the same stream k^1 as the H2D(g+1), stream ordering guarantees the copy finishes before the kernel runs, so no explicit sync is needed there. {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793152532955,"sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","part":{"id":"prt_18037e6a20015FqcIofYKYNWJG","messageID":"msg_18037e02a001q50tXcZ7XkBU8g","sessionID":"ses_e7fecd7c5ffeHgIqWUiMnKJKhn","type":"reasoning","text":"Kernel time totals 11.6s per rank with memcpy H2D around 4.3s total, seemingly reasonable bandwidth-wise. But that 29s cudaFreeHost cost stands out sharply — I need to check whether that's happening at the end of computeFormFactors, which would explain a lot of unaccounted time.\n\nThe precomputation phase itself includes a timeDelayKernel taking 5.5s for roughly 2×10^8 threads, which seems far too slow for a simple ceiling/sqrt computation — suggesting the memory access pattern isn't coalesced well. That's likely contributing heavily to the bottleneck alongside the suspicious cudaFreeHost stall.\n\nThat math doesn't add up either, so the slowness must come from elsewhere. I'm wondering if the cudaFreeHost time of 29s roughly matches the overall precompute total, which makes me suspect the reported kernel \"Time\" values from nsys aren't actual wall-clock durations but something else entirely, and I should reconsider what's really consuming the 28 seconds.\n\nThat doesn't add up either, unless nsys attributes exit-time cudaFreeHost calls into the same window. The cudaHostAlloc total of 149 ms for 2 calls seems reasonable, but cudaFreeHost totaling 57 s is still puzzling and needs more digging.\n\nActually, I misread the units - 63,896,401 ns is 63.9 ms, not seconds, so cudaFreeHost is actually just 64 ms total, consistent with cudaHostAlloc at 149 ms and cudaMemcpy at 76 ms. That means the 28 s precomputation breaks down as 5.5 s time delay plus 11.6 s FF kernels, leaving roughly 11 s of host-side work - likely the pass-1 skip computation and the partner computation loop running on the host.\n\nTrying to understand why the time delay kernel takes 5.5 s: the division by L shouldn't be that expensive given the thread count, and even accounting for poorly coalesced triangle loads from global memory, the bandwidth math suggests something closer to 20 ms, not 5.5 seconds, so there must be another bottleneck I'm missing in that kernel.\n\n64-bit division adds overhead but shouldn't account for seconds. The thread count also seems reasonable given block sizes, so speculating further isn't productive — I should just check the actual nsys kernel timing breakdown instead of guessing.\n\nActually, switching to 32-bit indices could help since all the N×L and N×N products stay comfortably under the uint32 limit, which would let the kernels use faster division. I'll try that change and remeasure rather than continuing to theorize.\n\nSeparately, I'm estimating the host-side round generation cost: with only K=12 threads actually doing work out of 128 available, each round's random number generation takes roughly 4-5ms, and across 853 rounds that adds up to several seconds of unaccounted host time.\n\nAdding in the skipped rows for the non-owned portion of the window brings host work to roughly 10ms per round, which is now close to overlapping the GPU kernel's 13ms, so it's roughly balanced. I'm thinking about whether parallelizing over elements within a row rather than over rows would help when K is small, though the sequential nature of the random engine per row complicates that.\n\nSince parallelism within a row isn't feasible without more snapshots, I decide the better path is to increase K (rows per rank per round) for more host-thread parallelism. I settle on targeting a buffer around 2^20 pairs-slots, which gives roughly 268MB per buffer and about 537MB total across both pinned host and device buffers — a reasonable size across varying N values like 20480 or 5120.\n\nFor small N, like 320, K needs to be capped at min(2^20/N, ceil(N/P)) to avoid overshooting. With K=51 for N=20480, I get about 201 rounds total, cutting down synchronization overhead. Checking occupancy, N*K gives roughly 1M threads per round, and scaling the earlier kernel timing (13ms for 245k threads) suggests about 52ms per round at this scale — consistent per-pair throughput. I'll move forward using 32-bit index math in the kernel with 2^20 as the target K.\n\n","time":{"start":1793152509602,"end":1793152532855},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

Two changes follow from that:\n\n- The time-delay kernel indexes with 64-bit `size_t` division.
